messages.subject: aboot on matrix object
parts:
I have succesfully applied the function aboot on genind, genclone, and genpop objects. However, as I am working with dominant markers I would like to obtain a tree with bootstrap support from allele frequencies estimated by AFLPsurv. 
According to the manual, aboot might be applied on a matrix object, but using a matrix of allele frequencies instead of a genpop object produces an error message.
Is it possible to prepare the matrix with allelic frequency data to be run with aboot?
Thaks for the comments
Juan

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] aboot on matrix object
parts:
Hi Juan,

I apologize, but I believe that is a mistake on my part. The function does not support matrices. I believe I put that in because functions such as nei.dist do support matrices. This will be cleared up in the next version.

Luckily, since each column represents a separate locus, you can perform your bootstrap with the package ape.

There are four steps:

1. create a tree generating function e.g. myTreeFun <- function(x){ nj(nei.dist(x)) } # This will calculate Nei's distance and then create a neighbor-joining tree. You can change the distance or tree function if you wish.
2. calculate the tree for your observed data: myTree <- myTreeFun(myData)
3. use the observed data, tree, and tree function with the ape function "boot.phylo":
node_labels <- ape::boot.phylo(x = myData, phy = myTree, FUN = myTreeFun, B = 1000)
4. add the node labels to your tree: myTree$node.labels <- node_labels

Hope that helps,
Zhian

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] aboot on matrix object
parts:
As pointed out in a private email thread, it is possible to create a genpop object with adegenet::genpop() from the matrix itself and use that to perform the bootstrap. I have also issued a fix to allow aboot to take matrix objects in the most recent development version of poppr. You can install it using the instructions here: https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr/tree/devel#stable-and-development-versions

devtools::install_github(repo = "grunwaldlab/poppr@devel")

Zhian
